tx-sc-chief-2026-blacklock-jimmy.name: Jimmy Blacklock
tx-sc-chief-2026-blacklock-jimmy.bio: Chief Justice of the Texas Supreme Court since 2025 and a justice on the court since 2018; former top lawyer to Governor Greg Abbott.

positions.stance: A judge should "apply the text of the law and the original meaning of the Constitution," never substituting personal decisions for those already made by the People of Texas.
Committed on the bench to applying the law "fairly, equally, and according to its original meaning."

tx-sc-chief-2026-ellis-maggie.name: Maggie Ellis
tx-sc-chief-2026-ellis-maggie.bio: Justice on the Texas Third Court of Appeals; former administrative law judge, prosecutor, trial attorney and public school teacher.

positions.stance: Her philosophy: "in matters of truth and justice, there is no difference between large and small problems, for issues concerning the treatment of people are all the same."

tx-sc-2-2026-sullivan-james.name: James P. Sullivan
tx-sc-2-2026-sullivan-james.bio: Texas Supreme Court justice appointed in January 2025; former General Counsel to Governor Greg Abbott.

tx-sc-2-2026-kelly-chari.name: Chari Kelly
tx-sc-2-2026-kelly-chari.bio: Justice on the Texas Third Court of Appeals since 2018; former U.S. Army JAG officer and prosecutor.

positions.stance: Says Texans deserve a Supreme Court that "reflects the people it serves, applies the law consistently, and puts justice over politics."

tx-sc-7-2026-hawkins-kyle.name: Kyle Hawkins
tx-sc-7-2026-hawkins-kyle.bio: Justice on the Supreme Court of Texas, appointed by Governor Greg Abbott.

positions.stance: Says the Court's work "demands humility, diligence, and a commitment to applying the law as written."

tx-sc-8-2026-busby-brett.name: Brett Busby
tx-sc-8-2026-busby-brett.bio: Texas Supreme Court justice since 2019; former justice on the Fourteenth Court of Appeals and former partner at Bracewell LLP.

positions.stance: Applies laws "faithfully to all who come before the Court—never rewriting those laws from the bench."
"Every decision must be grounded in the law, not politics, pressure, or personal preference."

tx-cca-3-2026-smith-thomas.name: Thomas Smith
tx-cca-3-2026-smith-thomas.bio: Attorney who served for a decade in the office of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

positions.stance: Seeks to restore "a conservative, limited judicial philosophy" to the court and opposes judges "making law from the bench."

tx-cca-3-2026-anyiam-okey.name: Okey Anyiam
tx-cca-3-2026-anyiam-okey.bio: Criminal defense attorney practicing primarily in North Texas, licensed in Texas since 1997.

positions.stance: Aims to "uphold the law without legislating from the bench, and to apply the clear legislative intent unless that intent is ambiguous."

tx-cca-9-2026-messinger-john.name: John Messinger
tx-cca-9-2026-messinger-john.bio: Career appellate prosecutor at the Office of the State Prosecuting Attorney.

positions.stance: Says improvement in justice comes not from judges doing what they think right but from "enforcing the laws as written to find out what works and what doesn't."

tx-cca-9-2026-taylor-holly.name: Holly Taylor
tx-cca-9-2026-taylor-holly.bio: Criminal defense attorney and former Travis County prosecutor of more than 17 years.

positions.stance: Believes "we must safeguard the independence, impartiality, and integrity of our Texas courts," ensuring all are treated "with dignity and humanity."
Says she will make tough decisions "with independence, impartiality, and integrity—without bending to political influence."

tx-coa15-chief-2026-brister-scott.name: Scott Brister
tx-coa15-chief-2026-brister-scott.bio: Inaugural Chief Justice of the Fifteenth Court of Appeals since 2024; former Texas Supreme Court justice and Harris County district judge.

positions.stance: Every party deserves "an impartial judge who applies the law, not personal beliefs or political preferences."
"Judges are not lawmakers"; his approach is to follow the law as written, respect the Constitution, and issue clear, reasoned decisions.

tx-coa15-chief-2026-zimmerer-jerry.name: Jerry Zimmerer
tx-coa15-chief-2026-zimmerer-jerry.bio: Former Justice on the 14th Court of Appeals in Houston (2018–2024) and Houston litigator.

positions.stance: "A court is only as trustworthy as the independence of the people sitting on it."

tx-coa15-2-2026-field-scott.name: Scott K. Field
tx-coa15-2-2026-field-scott.bio: Justice on the Fifteenth Court of Appeals since 2024; former judge of the 480th District Court and justice on the Third Court of Appeals.

positions.stance: Believes in "applying the law as written—not rewriting it to fit personal views or political outcomes."
Says Texans deserve a judiciary that is "independent, even-handed, and faithful to our Constitution."

tx-coa15-2-2026-baker-tom.name: Tom Baker
tx-coa15-2-2026-baker-tom.bio: Former justice on the Texas Third Court of Appeals (2019–2024); former U.S. Naval Reserve JAG officer and Bee County assistant county attorney.

positions.stance: The judiciary "must remain impartial and ensure that each branch acts within its 'constitutional lanes' to ensure fairness to all and deference to none."
Approaches every case with one guiding principle: "listen carefully, follow the law, and treat people fairly."

tx-coa15-3-2026-farris-april.name: April Farris
tx-coa15-3-2026-farris-april.bio: Justice on the Fifteenth Court of Appeals since 2024; former First Court of Appeals justice and Assistant Solicitor General of Texas.

positions.stance: Believes "judges should interpret the law as written—not rewrite it."
Says her role "is not to impose personal views or policy preferences, but to fairly and consistently apply the law in every case."

tx-coa15-3-2026-meyer-marc.name: Marc M. Meyer
tx-coa15-3-2026-meyer-marc.bio: Board-certified administrative law attorney; former Houston Fire Department captain and paramedic, and registered nurse.

positions.stance: Believes "the power of the state must always be tempered by the rights of the individual."

nc-supreme-court-seat-1-2026-earls-anita.name: Anita Earls
nc-supreme-court-seat-1-2026-earls-anita.bio: North Carolina Supreme Court associate justice since 2018; civil rights attorney and founder of the Southern Coalition for Social Justice.

positions.stance: As Justice, has continued "to uphold the rights enshrined in our State Constitution — like access to healthcare, a sound basic public education, and the right to vote."

nc-supreme-court-seat-1-2026-stevens-sar.name: Sarah Stevens
nc-supreme-court-seat-1-2026-stevens-sar.bio: Attorney in private practice for over 30 years and former Speaker Pro Tempore of the North Carolina House.

positions.stance: Believes "the law should be applied as written and judges shouldn't create laws from the bench."

nc-court-of-appeals-seat-1-2026-byrne-mi.name: Michael C. Byrne
nc-court-of-appeals-seat-1-2026-byrne-mi.bio: Administrative Law Judge for more than five years and former attorney practicing before the Office of Administrative Hearings.

positions.stance: Says conservative judges "apply the law, not 'make' the law" and "protect the rights in our North Carolina Constitution."
Issues decisions "strictly based on due process and the law, without fear or favor."

nc-court-of-appeals-seat-1-2026-arrowood.name: John S. Arrowood
nc-court-of-appeals-seat-1-2026-arrowood.bio: Judge on the North Carolina Court of Appeals since 2017; former Special Superior Court Judge and law firm partner.

nc-court-of-appeals-seat-2-2026-bell-geo.name: George Cooper Bell
nc-court-of-appeals-seat-2-2026-bell-geo.bio: Superior Court Judge in Judicial District 26C since 2019.

nc-court-of-appeals-seat-2-2026-hampson-.name: Tobias (Toby) Hampson
nc-court-of-appeals-seat-2-2026-hampson-.bio: Judge on the North Carolina Court of Appeals since 2018; former appellate practice group leader at Wyrick, Robbins, Yates & Ponton.

positions.stance: Says he "will work to protect our rights while remaining fair and impartial."

nc-court-of-appeals-seat-3-2026-collins-.name: Craig Collins
nc-court-of-appeals-seat-3-2026-collins-.bio: Superior Court Judge; former District Court judge, assistant district attorney and private-practice attorney.

nc-court-of-appeals-seat-3-2026-walczyk-.name: Christine Marie Walczyk
nc-court-of-appeals-seat-3-2026-walczyk-.bio: Wake County District Court judge for 19 years; former private-practice attorney in Raleigh.

positions.stance: Endeavors "to apply the law equally, without favoritism or bias"; says race, gender, sexual orientation and socio-economic status should not affect a case's outcome.
"Judges are not politicians"; they protect constitutional and statutory rights "without bending to political attacks, special interest, or public opinion."
Believes "an independent judiciary is the most crucial piece of a lasting democracy."
Says judges have a greater responsibility to serve neighbors and "increase the public's access to the justice system."

mi-sbe-2026-tilley-tiffany.name: Tiffany Tilley
mi-sbe-2026-tilley-tiffany.bio: Member of the Michigan State Board of Education since 2018; educator, author and adjunct professor.

positions.stance: Will keep fighting for "strong neighborhood schools, responsible investment, meaningful accountability, and the resources students need to succeed."
Wants strong literacy instruction for students and training, tools and support for educators to help "every child become a confident reader."
Will advocate for a funding system based on student need; "A child's ZIP code should never determine their opportunity."
Supports building a stronger pipeline into teaching and improving conditions so talented teachers and staff stay: "Recruit them. Support them. Keep them."
Every student should have access to rigorous academics, career and technical education, STEM, the arts, dual enrollment, skilled trades, and college pathways.
